The list below, however, is a *sibling* of the strip, not a descendant, so nothing scrolls it. Since that constraint is easy to forget, it would be better to encode/document it here instead of relying on callers.

comments.content:
`linesPerItem` is derived from the span mix of the *visible window*, but it is then applied to every item of the list, and it is multiplied by `avgHeight`, which is an average height per *item* — not per *line*. The two factors are inconsistent as soon as the window contains full-line items (`GridItemSpan(maxLineSpan)` banners/headers in AppsScreen).

Concrete failure: with `lanes = 3`, a viewport showing only 4 full-line items of 120 px gives `lineSpanSum/lanes = 4` lines over 4 items → `linesPerItem = 1`, so for 300 items `estimatedLines = 300` and `avgHeight = 120` ⇒ ~36000 px, while the real content is ≈ (300/3)×180 ≈ 18000 px. The scrollbar thumb is therefore up to ~2× too short at the top and visibly grows/shrinks while scrolling as banners enter/leave the window.

Suggestion: derive the height per *line* (group the visible items into lines, since they are ordered by index and a line ends when the accumulated span reaches `lanes`, taking the max height per line), or otherwise extrapolate from a window-independent quantity, instead of combining a span-weighted line count with a per-item average height.
